envelope.name: Envelope
envelope.title: External insulation · high-performance windows · shading
envelope.desc: Stops heat escaping through walls and windows — usually the first measure for older, heating-heavy low-rise buildings.

systems.name: Systems
systems.short: Heat pump · ventilation · LED · carport solar
systems.title: Heat pump · heat-recovery ventilation · LED · carport solar
systems.desc: Produces the same heat and light with less energy. Works well even where the envelope is hard to change.

roof.name: Roof · renewables
roof.title: Roof insulation · cool roof · solar PV
roof.desc: A large roof leaks heat — and is the best place for a power plant. Insulate it, then generate the building's own electricity.

operations.name: Operations
operations.title: Optimized operation with BEMS
operations.desc: Savings without construction: metering data reveals waste, and BEMS manages HVAC, standby power and lighting automatically.

envelope.title: Thermal imaging
envelope.desc: Find where the walls leak heat. Slab edges (thermal bridges) and window frames show up hottest.

systems.title: Systems audit
systems.desc: Check the efficiency of the old boiler and AC units, the ventilation and the lighting load.

roof.title: Roof thermal scan
roof.desc: Find a roof that bakes in summer and loses heat in winter.

operations.title: Metering · sensors
operations.desc: Power and HVAC meters on every floor show when and where energy is wasted.

insulation.title: External insulation
insulation.desc: Wrap the walls from outside with 100 mm phenolic foam boards to close the paths heat escapes through.

windows.title: High-performance windows
windows.desc: Low-E double glazing in insulated frames cuts the heat moving through the windows.

shading.title: External shading
shading.desc: Louvers come down when summer sun is strong to cut cooling, and let winter sun in.

heatpump.title: Heat pump
heatpump.desc: Replace the old gas boiler and AC units with air-source heat pumps that make the same heat with less energy.

erv.title: Heat-recovery ventilation
erv.desc: Transfer heat from outgoing air to incoming fresh air, so ventilation loses less heat.

led.title: LED lighting
led.desc: Replace fluorescent lamps with LEDs and halve the lighting load.

roofIns.title: Roof insulation · cool roof
roofIns.desc: Lay insulation on the roof and cover it with a bright, sun-reflecting finish.

pv.title: Solar PV
pv.desc: Put solar modules on the roof to generate the electricity the building uses.

schedule.title: Run hours · set points
schedule.desc: Run HVAC to the occupied hours and set 20 °C heating · 26 °C cooling.

standby.title: Standby power cut-off
standby.desc: Find equipment left on after hours, floor by floor, and switch it off.

lighting.title: Automatic lighting control
lighting.desc: Switch off lights automatically in empty hours and areas.

carportPv.title: Carport solar
carportPv.desc: Solar modules on the parking-lot carports shade the cars and generate the building's electricity.

panel.footnote: Example buildings recalculated after each step with Seoul weather (EnergyPlus 9.0). Results for a real building depend on its diagnosis.

method.title: Where the numbers come from
method.desc: The four buildings are examples, not real buildings. With the same Seoul weather (2009–2023 typical year), each retrofit step was added in turn and a full year simulated in EnergyPlus 9.0.
items: Primary energy uses Korea's building energy rating factors (electricity 2.75 · gas 1.1); carbon uses 0.4781 (electricity) · 0.2022 (LNG) kgCO₂/kWh.
Before: old walls (U 1.4 W/m²K), windows (4.0), roof (0.8), gas boiler efficiency 80–85%, cooling COP 2.6–3.0, fluorescent lighting 12 W/m².

After: 100 mm phenolic external insulation, Low-E double glazing (1.5), roof U 0.15 with reflective finish, heat pump (heating COP 3.2 · cooling 4.0), 70% heat recovery, LED 6 W/m², solar on 45% of the roof, 13.8 kW of carport solar (32 modules, 10° south).
Operations (BEMS): HVAC running 1 h before and 2 h after occupied hours trimmed to the occupied hours, set points 22/24 °C → 20/26 °C, after-hours standby 30% → 15%, lights left on 20% → 5%.
Improved airtightness from new windows is not counted (conservative), and fan and pump energy is excluded.
